questions.stem: In the disappearing cross experiment, the rate is proportional to 1/time. If the cross disappears in 40 seconds in one trial and 20 seconds in another, how do the rates compare?

options.text: Both trials have the same rate
The second trial is twice as fast
The second trial is four times as fast
The second trial is half as fast

questions.explanation: Rate is proportional to 1/time. For the first trial: rate = 1/40 = 0.025 s⁻¹. For the second trial: rate = 1/20 = 0.05 s⁻¹. The second trial has double the rate (0.05/0.025 = 2), meaning the reaction was twice as fast.
